facts.claim: "Feel Something" is a single by American DJ Illenium, Canadian producer Excision and American rock band I Prevail, released April 3, 2020 on Astralwerks.
The track was produced by Illenium, David Pramik and Excision.
Illenium and Excision were working on a then-untitled single in the studio in July 2019. They debuted "Feel Something" in September 2019 during a back-to-back set at Lost Lands.
The track closed Illenium and Excision's first-ever b2b set at Excision's Lost Lands festival at Legend Valley.
Excision said in a tweet that the song was made in the studio after the Global Dance Festival was canceled.
I Prevail's Brian Burkheiser sings the chorus. Eric Vanlerberghe contributes screamed vocals.
Soundazed described the track as combining melodic dubstep from Illenium, glitch-hop from Excision, and vocals from I Prevail's lead vocalist.
It is the second Illenium and Excision collaboration, following their 2018 track "Gold (Stupid Love)". Heard It Here First called it darker, more of an indie-rock hybrid than a dance-pop one.
The lyric video, published April 3, 2020, features Illenium as a phoenix and Excision as a dinosaur.
The track reached number eight on Billboard's Hot Dance/Electronic Songs chart.

research.lineage: The song sits in the crossover of melodic dubstep and heavy bass music with metalcore and rock vocals, pairing Illenium's emotional melodic style with Excision's aggressive dubstep.

draft:
"I don't pray to God but I did today." **Feel Something** opens on a confession that undoes itself mid-line, a nonbeliever caught asking anyway. It doesn't feel like faith returning. It feels like someone so worn down that any outlet will do, and the next lines say why: "'Cause I'm scared that I believe in nothin'." The fear isn't of pain. It's of the flatness under it, the suspicion that nothing will answer back.

That's an odd and brave thing to build a bass-music single around. Illenium and Excision made it in the studio after the Global Dance Festival was canceled, Excision said, and they debuted it in September 2019 as the closer of their first back-to-back set at Lost Lands, Excision's own festival. Soundazed heard the split clearly: Illenium's melodic dubstep, Excision's glitch-hop, and I Prevail supplying the voice. It's their second collaboration after "Gold (Stupid Love)," and Heard It Here First called it the darker one, leaning toward an indie-rock hybrid instead of dance-pop. The track sits where melodic dubstep's big emotional swells meet metalcore's habit of letting the chorus soar and the screams tear it open.

Brian Burkheiser sings the chorus in a clean, clear tone that strains at the edges, doubled so it lands as a small chorus of selves. Under him, a sustained synth pad hangs in the air, kick and snare hold a steady, deliberate beat, and the bass stays simple and low. The production is polished and roomy, and the arrangement keeps stacking toward something heavier while the voice climbs. Eric Vanlerberghe's screamed vocals bring the other half of the argument, the part of the feeling that can't stay melodic.

The verse holds two stances at once. "Guess I only have myself to blame" is a shrug at self-blame, half accepted and half resented. A line later the narrator wonders whether to let go and then admits, "I'm afraid to let go." Release is wanted and dreaded in the same breath, and the song never settles it. The chorus turns that stalemate into a bargain: anything, everything, for one real sensation.

Then the language wears down. Past the chorus the lyric shrinks to "I just wanna feel," repeated, and finally to wordless "oh"s, as if words were the first thing numbness takes. On a festival field that becomes a crowd singing vowels together, which may be the closest thing to an answer the song offers: you aren't on your own if thousands of people are aching the same way. It reached number eight on Billboard's Hot Dance/Electronic Songs chart.

The song works because it doesn't ask you to feel better, only to feel at all, and that's a much easier prayer to join in on.
